meetingTitle: Raffles Place Flagship & App Promo Launch

card.youAre: You are Wei Ling, Operations Director looking after the shop floor, Auntie Mary, food hygiene, and the budget.
facts: We have 10 stools in the storeroom to set up a Laptop & Solo Window Bar, and we can switch off booth wall plugs from 8–10 AM with table signs so 62-year-old Auntie Mary never has to confront anyone.
Our head chef caught the unplugged fridge at 6 AM, threw out all the old food with a signed disposal receipt, and restocked with fresh supplies delivered this morning.
We only lose $0.40 on single $10 delivery sets—switching GrabFood to $50 Office Platters (5-set bundles) makes $5 profit per platter even after the 32% fee without pulling staff off the counter.
The kiosk has a 'Subtitle Mode' that shows plain English ('Black Coffee, No Sugar') on screen for customers while still printing traditional Kopi names on the kitchen ticket for Uncle Lim.
card.responsibility: Make sure our plans work for Auntie Mary and the counter staff without breaking food hygiene or losing money.

card.youAre: You are Arjun, Tech & POS Lead looking after the self-order kiosks, the kitchen ticket printer, and store power.
facts: The kiosk has a 'Subtitle Mode' we can turn on in 2 minutes—it shows plain English ('Black Coffee, No Sugar') on screen while still printing 'Kopi O Kosong' on Uncle Lim's kitchen ticket.
The booth wall sockets run on a back-room switch we can auto-turn off from 8–10 AM, while keeping power on at the 10-stool window bar for laptop users.
GrabFood hides shops that raise single-item prices online, but adding a $50 Office Platter (5-set bundle) keeps our store visible and makes $5 profit per platter.
Our head chef caught the unplugged fridge at 6 AM, logged the disposal receipt, and loaded fresh morning supplies.
card.responsibility: Keep the kiosks, kitchen printer, and store power simple enough to configure and test tonight.

card.youAre: You are Mei, Menu & Store Experience Lead looking after our kopi and kaya toast recipes, the menu, and customer flow.
facts: The kiosk has a 'Subtitle Mode' that shows plain English ('Black Coffee, No Sugar') under 'Kopi O Kosong' on screen while still printing traditional Kopi names in the kitchen.
Our head chef caught the warm fridge at 6 AM, threw out all the old stock with a signed receipt, and loaded fresh morning supplies so we don't have to pull breakfast sets.
We have 10 stools in the storeroom to open a Window Bar for laptop users and solo diners carrying hot trays, plus table signs for the main dining booths.
Switching GrabFood to $50 Office Platters (5-set bundles) uses shared trays and makes $5 profit per platter even after Grab's 32% fee.
card.responsibility: Keep our kopi and kaya toast authentic while making ordering and finding a seat easier.

card.youAre: You are Daniel, Marketing Lead looking after TikTok reviews, store promos, and public goodwill.
facts: Our store insurance covers up to $3,000 in immediate no-fault medical goodwill for the hospitalized customer's family, and our head chef has the 6 AM disposal receipt for the old fridge stock.
12 nearby Raffles Place offices asked for a 10%-off direct self-pickup code, and switching GrabFood to $50 Office Platters (5-set bundles) makes $5 profit per platter even after the 32% fee.
Moving laptop users to the 10-stool window bar with table signs protects our Google reviews without forcing Auntie Mary to police tables.
Turning on Kiosk 'Subtitle Mode' clears the doorway queue before the landlord fines us $2,000, while keeping traditional Kopi names on Uncle Lim's kitchen tickets.
card.responsibility: Protect our launch reputation and nearby office orders without making promises the kitchen or floor staff cannot keep.

card.youAre: You are Sam, General Manager chairing the huddle.
facts: Call on the lead for each topic and let the team hash out the practical catches.
Make sure each topic wraps up with a clear call and someone owning the follow-up.
card.responsibility: Chair the huddle, hear both sides out, and assign a follow-up owner for each topic.

agenda.title: First-timers stalling at the kiosk over Kopi names
agenda.decision: how do we clear the 25-person kiosk line before the building landlord fines us $2,000, without making 65-year-old Uncle Lim walk out of the kitchen?

openingViews.view: The building landlord just threatened to fine us $2,000 because 25 newcomers are blocking the entrance lobby staring at 'Kopi O Kosong' on the kiosk. Can't we just change the screen buttons to plain English like 'Black Coffee' and 'Latte' right now?
Hold on—65-year-old Uncle Lim in the kitchen said if his order tickets start printing 'Latte' instead of 'Kopi', he's taking off his apron and walking out!
Yeah, whatever button name we put on the screen prints straight onto Uncle Lim's ticket by default, and our screen only fits 12 buttons unless we turn on Subtitle Mode or change how people queue.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: $2,000 landlord fine & lobby jam: 25 tourists and office newcomers are blocking the building doorway because they freeze at 'Kopi O Kosong'.
tradeOffs.question: How do we help newcomers order fast and clear the doorway before the landlord fines us $2,000?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Uncle Lim threatening to walk out: 65-year-old Uncle Lim refuses to read 'Latte' on kitchen tickets and slows down by 15 seconds a cup on English tickets.
tradeOffs.question: How do we keep traditional Kopi names on Uncle Lim's kitchen tickets so he doesn't walk out?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Kiosk screen & ticket setup: Renaming buttons changes the kitchen ticket too, unless we enable Kiosk Subtitle Mode or put a staff member at the door.
tradeOffs.question: Should we enable Kiosk Subtitle Mode, station a queue-buster at the door, or split the line?

agenda.title: Morning seat crunch & laptop campers
agenda.decision: how do we free up tables for breakfast customers and stop 62-year-old Auntie Mary from quitting on the spot, without triggering 1-star Google reviews?

openingViews.view: Half our tables are blocked for two hours by people on laptops who only bought a $2 coffee, and 62-year-old Auntie Mary is crying in the back threatening to quit after a guy in a suit screamed at her! I say we ban laptops and cut all power plugs during breakfast!
Whoa, hold on—half those laptop users work in the offices upstairs, so if we kick them out rudely on Opening Day, they'll tank our Google rating with 1-star reviews.
Plus 60% of our paying walk-ins come alone carrying scalding hot trays of eggs and kopi—they need a guaranteed spot to sit without Auntie Mary having to police anyone.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Auntie Mary threatening to quit: 62-year-old Auntie Mary is in tears after a customer in a suit yelled at her, and she will quit today if forced to police tables.
tradeOffs.question: How do we protect Auntie Mary so she never has to confront laptop campers again?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: 16 blocked seats & hot trays: Laptop campers hold 16 of 28 seats on one $2 drink while solo diners carrying hot trays walk out.
tradeOffs.question: Where do we put laptop users and solo diners so paying breakfast customers have seats?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Office regular backlash: Kicking upstairs office workers out rudely risks a wave of 1-star Google reviews on launch day.
tradeOffs.question: Do we move laptops to the 10-stool window bar with table signs, set a minimum spend, or cut booth plugs from 8–10 AM?

agenda.title: SFA food safety inspection & salmonella report
agenda.decision: how do we handle the hospitalized customer, the part-time cleaner who unplugged the fridge, and the 9 AM health inspection?

openingViews.view: A customer from yesterday's trial is in the hospital with food poisoning because our new part-time night cleaner unplugged the fridge for three hours to charge his phone! Health inspectors arrive at 9 AM—do we fire the cleaner, and how do we pass inspection without losing $1,800 in morning sales?

The customer's angry family is threatening to blast us online and Straits Times reporters arrive at 8 AM—we need to decide if we pay their hospital bill right now or shut the kitchen down for the morning!
Wait—our head chef caught the warm fridge at 6 AM, threw out all the old food with a signed disposal receipt, and loaded fresh morning supplies, so we don't have to close if we're upfront!

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Hospitalized customer & 8 AM press: The patient's family is furious and reporters arrive at 8 AM; our insurance covers up to $3,000 in medical goodwill.
tradeOffs.question: How do we take care of the hospitalized customer's family and answer the 8 AM reporters?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Unplugged fridge & 9 AM health inspection: A part-time cleaner unplugged the fridge for 3 hours, and health inspectors arrive at 9 AM.
tradeOffs.question: What do we do about the part-time cleaner, and what do we show the 9 AM health inspector?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Kitchen opening vs $1,800 sales: Closing the kitchen loses $1,800 this morning, while the chef already replaced the spoiled stock with fresh 6 AM supplies.
tradeOffs.question: Do we stay open using this morning's fresh delivery and 6 AM disposal receipt, or pause the kitchen?

agenda.title: Delivery platform 32% commission squeeze
agenda.decision: how do we stop losing $0.40 on every GrabFood order when 40 rainy-day orders are queued and riders are blocking the counter?

openingViews.view: GrabFood hiked their commission to 32% overnight so we're losing 40 cents on every $10 breakfast set—and because it's pouring rain, 40 office orders just came in at once! We can't just cancel 40 orders on Opening Day or those offices will boycott us!
If we raise single-set prices on GrabFood, their app hides our store in search—and 15 wet delivery riders are already jamming our walk-in counter!
We can't bleed 40 cents per order all morning, and my two counter staff can't leave the toast line—unless we switch the app to $50 Office Platters that actually make $5 profit!

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Losing $0.40 per single order: Grab's 32% cut makes single $10 sets lose $0.40, while $50 Office Platters (5-set bundles) make $5 profit per platter.
tradeOffs.question: Do we switch the app to $50 Office Platters, turn off GrabFood, or eat the loss on single sets today?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: 40 rainy-day orders & $2,400 office sales: Cancelling queued orders in the rain triggers an office boycott, while 12 nearby offices want a 10%-off direct pickup code.
tradeOffs.question: How do we handle the 40 queued rainy-day orders and keep the nearby offices ordering from us?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Riders jamming the walk-in counter: 15 delivery riders are blocking walk-in customers, and raising single-set prices on Grab hides our shop.
tradeOffs.question: How do we update the online menu and keep delivery riders from blocking our walk-in counter?

situation: We reopen our refurbished Nanyang Kopi & Toast flagship at Raffles Place tomorrow at 8:00 AM.

glossary.Kopi O Kosong: black coffee with no sugar and no milk
glossary.Teh C Siew Dai: hot tea with evaporated milk and less sugar
glossary.chope: reserving a kopitiam table by leaving a packet of tissue paper or lanyard on it
glossary.Set A: kaya butter toast with two soft-boiled eggs and a hot kopi or tea
glossary.POS: point-of-sale system (the self-order kiosk, cashier screen, and kitchen ticket printer)
glossary.SFA: Singapore Food Agency (the national food hygiene and safety regulator)
glossary.Auntie Mary: our 62-year-old floor staff member who clears trays and wipes tables
glossary.kiosk: the 15-inch self-order touchscreens at the front of the outlet

hostBrief.goal: Hear out the team on today's four launch problems, stress-test surface-level ideas, and lock in a follow-up owner for each.
